Enumerate unions of full orbits (plus low-dimensional fixed seed orbits) whose distinct-point count is exactly 292, parametrize only the 3-4 coordinates of each seed point on $S^3$, and optimise this low-dimensional problem by log-sum-exp L-BFGS with $\alpha$ continued $50\to200\to1000$, deduplicating points closer than $10^{-8}$ and discarding orbit unions that cannot reach 292. Expand the best few symmetric candidates to full $(292,4)$ arrays, break symmetry with a tiny $10^{-4}$ tangent perturbation, LP-polish, and return the better of this and the loaded incumbent; a symmetric or near-symmetric basin, if competitive before polishing, is structurally different from the incumbent and may polish below it.

direction: Run contact-topology basin hopping with a novelty archive and non-greedy acceptance: define the topology as the sorted edge list of pairs with slack $<10^{-6}$, hash it, and maintain an archive of visited hashes plus their scores. Generate moves targeted by LP dual stress and loose-threshold degree: pick a high-stress edge or an over-coordinated point, delete 1-3 points from that stressed neighbourhood, and reinsert them sequentially at largest spherical holes found from 50,000 random candidates refined by local minimisation of max cosine to the current set; polish each candidate only cheaply (300 softmax steps plus LP capped at 2 s), reject immediately if its hash is already archived and its score is not better, and accept surviving worse candidates with simulated-annealing probability $\exp(-\Delta/T)$, $T$ decaying from $2\times10^{-6}$ to $10^{-8}$, restarting from `best.npy` only every 10 iterations. Fully LP-polish (20-30 s) only candidates whose hash is new and whose cheap score is within $2\times10^{-5}$ of the incumbent, so time is spent on different $\sim$870-edge graphs rather than re-polishing the known one.

Equalize the isostatic active set in tangent coordinates with exact Jacobian least-squares plus KKT multiplier pruning and line search.
direction: Perform high-precision active-set equalization instead of another softmax anneal: build a $292\times3$ orthonormal tangent basis at each $x_i$, take as active all pairs with slack $<5\times10^{-7}$ (expected $\sim$900 pairs, padded to the top 1200), and solve the equality problem $c_{ij}(y)-t=0$ for tangent coordinates $y$ and common level $t$ with `scipy.optimize.least_squares` (variables $876+1$, analytic Jacobian $x_j$ projected into $i$'s tangent basis and vice versa, `xtol=ftol=1e-15`), followed by an exact line search on the true max cosine. After each solve, compute LP/KKT multipliers for the active pairs, drop pairs with significantly negative multipliers, add any inactive pair violating the new $t$, and repeat until active slacks are $<10^{-12}$ or multipliers certify stationarity; only accept if the exact max improves, otherwise return the incumbent, using the remaining time for a final tight LP with initial radius $10^{-5}$ rather than $10^{-3}$.

idea: Stress-guided target feasibility that deactivates incompatible contacts and optimises a weighted softplus hinge below the record, then LP-polishes near-feasible basins.
direction: Use stress-guided target feasibility to force a topology change: assemble the Jacobian of the approximately 870 active contacts, solve for equilibrium stresses by least squares or extract LP dual multipliers, and select subsets of contacts with unusually large, negative, or otherwise incompatible stresses to deactivate. For target values $T=0.90340$, $0.90335$, and $0.90325$, optimise a smooth hinge objective $\sum_{i<j}\operatorname{softplus}(\beta(\langle x_i,x_j\rangle-T))^2$ while adding extra repulsion to the deactivated pairs so they must fall at least $10^{-5}$ below $T$; alternate L-BFGS/softmax optimisation with LP only after the smooth violation is small. Success at any $T$ immediately gives a better code, while near-feasible failures provide starting points whose active set is structurally different rather than another copy of the incumbent graph.

idea: Delete-insert ladder through neighbouring N with hole refilling and short LP re-polishing to change the jammed contact topology
direction: Search through neighbouring cardinalities $N=280$–$304$ as a topology-changing ladder: repeatedly remove the highest-stress or most over-contacted point from the 292-code, reoptimise the smaller code, then rebuild to 292 by inserting points one at a time into its largest optimised holes; also overshoot to $N=293$–$300$, reoptimise, and delete a different point from the one just inserted so the final 292-code follows a nontrivial delete–insert cycle. Branch this process over several deletion orders and hole choices, score intermediate codes only after LP polishing, and compare their contact graphs by sorted pair-slack signatures; this exploits the possibility that the natural basin for 292 is easier to reach from a relaxed neighbouring-$N$ configuration than from the already-jammed record.

direction: Detect and exploit latent approximate symmetry instead of imposing an arbitrary group: search for orthogonal transformations that nearly preserve the incumbent point set by aligning matched point neighbourhoods with Kabsch fits and measuring Hausdorff matching error, and in parallel test signed-permutation $B_4/D_4$ alignments in the best rotated coordinate frame. Snap the configuration to the best union of group orbits by averaging points over each approximate orbit, optimise only the orbit representatives with log-sum-exp continuation, and then release symmetry gradually through $X(\lambda)=\operatorname{normalize}((1-\lambda)X_{\rm sym}+\lambda X_{\rm free})$ for a grid of $\lambda$ values interleaved with short anneals and LP polishes. Keep intermediate symmetric or partly symmetric candidates based on contact-graph novelty and stress regularity—not only raw score—because the desired structure may be a symmetry-broken descendant of a regular orbit code rather than either the present asymmetric optimum or an exactly symmetric code.

idea: Delete-and-refill ladder through neighbouring N: remove hub/rattler points, relax the smaller code, then regrow to 292 via largest-hole insertion with smoothing and LP polish over multiple deletion orders.
direction: Search through neighbouring cardinalities $N=280$–$304$ as a topology-changing ladder: repeatedly remove the highest-stress or most over-contacted point from the 292-code, reoptimise the smaller code, then rebuild to 292 by inserting points one at a time into its largest optimised holes; also overshoot to $N=293$–$300$, reoptimise, and delete a different point from the one just inserted so the final 292-code follows a nontrivial delete–insert cycle. Branch this process over several deletion orders and hole choices, score intermediate codes only after LP polishing, and compare their contact graphs by sorted pair-slack signatures; this exploits the possibility that the natural basin for 292 is easier to reach from a relaxed neighbouring-$N$ configuration than from the already-jammed record.

idea: Metropolis basin-hopping that keeps worse moves to cross the slack gap, transplanting rattlers and high-degree points into empty caps with frozen-then-joint softmax annealing before short LP evaluation.
Clean-room algebraic and Riesz population with LSE continuation and graph-diversity archiving before final LP polish.
direction: Clean-room diverse population from algebraic seeds, with incumbent used only as a final fallback. Generate starting configurations that never load `best.npy`: (a) points derived from $D_4$ root/lattice shells and subsets or orbits of the 600-cell/24-cell mapped to 292 points, (b) random points optimised under Riesz energies with several exponents ($s=1,2,4,8$) before switching to the max-cosine objective, and (c) low-dimensional quaternion/cyclic orbit families with group orders and seed counts different from those already tried (e.g. orders 4, 8, 12 with mixed orbit sizes summing to 292, allowing a few free points). Polish each seed cheaply with log-sum-exp continuation $\alpha=30\to300\to1500$ (capped iterations), compute its contact-graph hash and degree histogram, and maintain an archive selected for graph diversity and near-six-regular degree balance rather than score alone. Only in the last ~30 s LP-polish the best two or three genuinely distinct graphs and return the best overall, falling back to the loaded incumbent if none beats it; this directly tests whether an unrelated, more balanced basin exists instead of re-deriving the known vertex.

idea: Stress-guided edge-flip search that audits the isostatic contact vertex via Jacobian SVD and systematically swaps low-stress contacts for near-contacts with targeted L-BFGS.
direction: Stress-audited edge-flip enumeration. Compute the contact set at tolerance $10^{-7}$ (expect ~870 pairs), build the $870\times876$ tangent-space Jacobian of those pairs, and find its (essentially unique) equilibrium stress vector $s$ via SVD null-space, sign-normalised so $\sum s>0$. Rank contacts by $s$; a genuinely improvable vertex should have contacts with negative or near-zero stress. Systematically enumerate candidate topology changes: for each of the $\sim$25 lowest-stress contacts to "release" and each of the $\sim$40 closest non-contact pairs to "force in", run a short L-BFGS optimisation (200-400 iterations, log-sum-exp with $\alpha$ ramping $300\to3000$) in which the forced pair is penalised toward a target cosine $T=\text{best}-3\times10^{-6}$ and the released pair is excluded from the active penalty, starting from the incumbent. LP-polish only candidates whose post-L-BFGS max cosine is below best $+2\times10^{-5}$, hash each candidate's contact graph, and keep any distinct graph even if only equal-scoring. Keep the code short, wrap every candidate in try/except, and always retain the loaded incumbent as the safe return value.

idea: Delete rattler plus 3 high/low-degree core points and jointly reinsert into massive quasi-random hole search with frozen-keep refinement then staged thaw (narrow to wide shells) using high-beta softmax annealing before LP polish.
direction: Rattler-and-core unlocking surgery with staged thawing. Identify the rattler and all points with degree $\le3$ or $\ge8$. Delete the rattler together with 2-3 of its would-be neighbours' highest-degree partners (3-4 points total), then reinsert the deleted points jointly: sample $\ge$50,000 quasi-random points on $S^3$, score each by its maximum cosine to the retained 288-289 points and to the other reinserted points, greedily pick well-separated hole points (mutual cosine also $\le T$), and locally refine them with the retained set frozen. Then thaw in stages — first only retained points within cosine $>0.55$ of a moved point, then a cosine $>0.2$ shell, then all points — using softmax annealing ($\beta: 100\to1500$, decaying step) at each stage before a final LP polish. Repeat with several deletion choices (rattler plus different high-degree points) and different random seeds, since the point is to let the over-braced core re-form with the rattler carrying ~6 contacts rather than to reinsert it into the old core.

idea: Jammed-to-void transplant search that moves overloaded contact points into large spherical holes with a Metropolis walker plus softmax annealing and LP polishing to balance degrees and eliminate the rattler.
